lessons.label: Reading 1
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Present simple to describe personality (e.g. I’m kind Sara.) and expectations (e.g. This year I want to…)

pre: Play vocabulary game to activate knowledge of words learned in previous years. Focus on word sets pupils will use in this lesson (personality adjectives, family, school subjects, free- time activities and holidays). Choose an activity from the pre-lesson task list in Section 3 of this document.
delivery: Introduce yourself and describe your personality with an adjective, e.g. Hi! I’m kind Sara. Have pupils brainstorm personality adjectives and introduce themselves in groups. Ask pupils to make name cards (this could be done at home) showing their personality and their name.

Ask the pre-reading question in the Teacher’s Book for Warm-up: The big picture (Where are they?). Then ask pupils to read the short texts in the Pupil’s Book, p.4. Ask pupils which of the children they agree with most and what they would like to learn about this year.

Ask for two or three volunteers to introduce themselves to the class using the texts as a model. Ask all pupils to introduce themselves to their partner, using the texts and the volunteers as a model. Monitor as pupils do this to get an impression of individuals’ levels in your class.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.18, for Activity 1. Pupils listen to the four children talking about themselves. Have them read the audio script as they listen.
Pupils read the script again. Ask a question to check their overall understanding of the text, for example: Which child are you similar to? Pupils tell their partner.
Ask pupils to note two things about themselves in their notebooks.
Using these notes and the personality adjective, ask pupils to write at least two sentences about themselves.
post: Pupils introduce themselves in new groups by reading their self-introduction.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 4–5 Exercise(s): 1 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 18-19 Copy the audio script for each pupil
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider asking some pupils to explain more about their personality, their expectations for the year and what they hope to contribute to the class (CCE: Values).

lessons.label: Listening 1
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Present simple for defining vocabulary (e.g. This is a person who…)

pre: Play a game to introduce the two topics (jobs & places), for example Beat the Teacher (see Pre-lesson Task 7).
delivery: Follow the instructions for Warm-up in the Teacher’s Book, p.20 – pupils listen to words and categorise them.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 (Teacher’s Book, p.20) – pupils find words in the picture.

Review answers to Step 3 by having pupils listen to the word and point to the picture. Drill the new words as they point. Focus on difficult sounds and word stress of longer words such as photographer, businesswoman and police officer. Ask pupils to count the syllables with their fingers and highlight the stressed syllable as they say the longer words.

Read aloud the definitions you have prepared. Pupils listen to your definitions and try to find the words you are describing. They should write the words. [E.g. This is a person who rides the waves on a board].
Check answers and draw attention to spelling where needed.
Have pupils prepare some similar definitions and play the game in small groups.
post: Review learning by asking pupils to say which words they often use in their own daily lives.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 6–7 Exercise(s): 1 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 20 Prepare 4 or 5 definitions for vocabulary items
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider pre- writing some definitions for less proficient pupils to choose from in Step 7.

lessons.label: Language Arts 1
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Reported speech (e.g. He said he sat in some glue.)

pre: Pupils look at the pictures around the poem and talk about them.
Pupils guess what the poem is about.
delivery: Recite the poem and pupils repeat after.
Pupils do gestures as they recite the poem e.g. jumping, kicking, thirsty, sticky
Elicit from the pupils on who they can relate to best: Jumping John, Kicking Kirsty, Mad Mickey or Fat Fred.
Demonstrate how to perform a jazz chant for the first stanza.
Help pupils to identify the stress and rhythm by clapping hands or snapping fingers in time to the beat.
In groups, pupils recite the poem in a form of a jazz chant.
post: Pupils assess each group’s recitation using Two Stars and a Wish: two things that are good (stars) and one thing that can be improved (wish).

lessons.materials: Anthology of Poems for Year 4,5, and 6 Messing About by Michael Rosen Page: 27 Contemporary Children’s Literature Teaching Guidebook (BPK) – Poetry
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils and class. Please see the seven differentiation strategies listed in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider pairing less with more proficient pupils, so they can help support each other in Step 8.

lessons.label: Reading 2
lessons.focus: Introduction to past simple & past continuous

pre: Write electricity on the board and have pupils brainstorm uses of electricity in small groups. This could be done as a game.
delivery: Elicit different meanings of the word power, including as a synonym for electricity. Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.22, for Activity 1. Pupils discuss the questions.
Talk to the pupils about prediction skills in reading (see ‘Teaching Star’, Teacher’s Book, p.22) and encourage prediction based on the pictures.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.23. Pupils analyse the text to decide on the text type.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.23. Pupils further analyse the text to identify different features of it.
Follow the instructions for Activity 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.23. Pupils search for words in the text and use context clues to guess meaning.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.24. Pupils look for detail in the text to answer questions.
Ask pupils to re-read the text to find something interesting and tell their partner.
Talk to pupils and lead a discussion about our increasing need for and reliance on electricity and power as we use more and more electronics (CCE: Global sustainability and Science & Technology).
post: 9. Follow instructions for the Cooler memory game activity in the Teacher’s Book, p.23.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 8–10 Exercise(s): 1–4; 1 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 22–24
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider giving step-by-step guidance at Step 6. This may be a new skill for pupils. If some of your pupils may find this difficult, you could give them alternative definitions to choose from or create a word- definition matching activity.

lessons.label: Writing 1
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Past simple & continuous for interrupted actions with when

pre: Briefly review the text from the previous lesson by asking some true/false questions. Then have pupils discuss the questions in Activity 3 (Pupil’s Book, p.10).
delivery: Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.26. Pupils see and analyse the new language.
Follow the instructions in ‘Personalisation’ in the Teacher’s Book, p.26. Pupils relate the new language to their own lives.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.26. Pupils read and choose the correct words.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.27. Pupils use prompts to make sentences.

Pupils work in pairs. They cut a piece paper into 6, 8 or 10 equal small pieces of paper using a grid. On each small piece of paper, they write a sentence in the past simple. Write an example on the board to show pupils what to do. They can use the examples in Activity 3 for ideas.

In pairs put the small papers together in a pile. In turns, they take two papers from the pile and try to make a sentence using the target language (e.g. I was xxx-ing when xxx.) Pupils write the sentences in their notebooks.
Have some pairs tell the class any funny sentences they made.
post: Choose a post-lesson task from Section 3 to review content and/or language pupils had difficulty with during the lesson.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 10–11 Exercise(s): 3; 1– 3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 26–27 Plain paper for each pupil Scissors
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. At Steps 3 and 6, differentiate by the number of sentences/cards pupils create.

lessons.label: Speaking 1
lessons.focus: Past simple & continuous for interrupted actions with when/while

pre: Use the clock/clock face to show different times. Ask pupils to tell their partner what they were doing at that time yesterday/on Saturday/etc. Monitor and remind pupils of the use of past continuous if necessary.
delivery: Introduce the pupils to the dictionary in the Pupil’s Book (see Vocabulary instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.28).
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.28. Pupils are introduced to the dialogue.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.28. Pupils read and complete the text with when or while.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, pp.28–29. Pupils match actions and activities.

Pupils work in pairs. They take one or two ideas from Activity 3 or from the unit as a whole, or they use their own ideas to create a story. Pupils make detailed notes about their story in pairs and practise telling their story. Remind pupils to use the target language with when and/or while.
post: Choose some pupils to tell their stories to the class. Have the class decide which story is most exciting/interesting/frightening etc. If you have a large class or time is short, pairs could tell their stories in larger groups.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 12 Exercise(s): 1–3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 28–29 A toy clock (or draw a clock face on the board before the lesson)
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider setting different limits/targets or minimum word limits/targets for different pairs, for example: Use at least 10 verbs/ Speak for at least 30 seconds.

lessons.label: Language Arts 2
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Nouns

pre: Give lyrics to pupils to sing along. (Refer to the guidebook)
Pupils listen to a short song about sandwich. http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wUDqQSwdBjM
delivery: Pupils recite the poem aloud with guidance .
Pupils call out the ingredients found in the poem.
Each pupil gets The Silly Sandwich template. (Handout 1)
Pupils write down 10 ingredients they wish to put in their Silly Sandwich.
Pupils draw the ingredients on The Silly Sandwich template.
post: Pupils present and explain their choice of ingredients.

lessons.materials: Anthology of Poems for Year 4,5, and 6 The Sandwich by Tony Bradman Page(s): 28-29 http://www.youtub e.com/watch?v=w UDqQSwdBjM Contemporary Children’s Literature Teaching Guidebook (BPK) – Poetry
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider giving a little more time to finish for some pupils who need longer than others to complete tasks, especially when writing is involved and extra tasks for pupils who complete the task early should be provided.

lessons.label: Writing 2
lessons.focus: Past simple & continuous for interrupted actions with when/while; Direct speech

pre: Play a mime game to review the words in Working with words (Pupil’s Book, p.15).
delivery: Follow the instructions for Working with words in the Teacher’s Book, p.32. Extend this activity with more examples if relevant, such as bored/boring; shocked/shocking.
Give pupils the worksheet. First, ask pupils to highlight the headline and underline any direct speech.
Next, pupils read the jumbled sections of the newspaper article and decide which paragraph(s) are the introduction/main body/conclusion.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.33 for the Workbook Activity 1 (see Activity 1 of Prepare to Write, p.14). Pupils order the pictures to tell a story.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.33 for the Workbook Activities 2 & 3. Pupils organise ideas into the main sections (introduction, main body, conclusion).

Follow instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.33 for the Workbook Activity 4, p.15. Pupils write a newspaper article. Remind pupils to include adjectives, direct speech and interrupted actions. Note that this activity helps pupils develop organisational and narrative skills for the Speaking Assessment, where they should narrate a story based on picture prompts.
post: Have pupils choose an adjective from Step 2 to make a sentence about their newspaper story. Remind pupils to bring their writing to the next lesson.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 15 Exercise(s): 3 & Working with words Workbook: Pages: 14–15 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 32-33
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. You could ask pupils to finish this at home if they don’t have time to complete it during the lesson.

lessons.label: Listening 2
lessons.focus: Should(n’t) for giving advice

pre: Review homework by asking pupils to review each other’s writing using the questions in Activity 5 on p.15 of the Workbook.
delivery: Follow instructions in the Teacher’s Book p.36 for the Warm-up activity. Pupils share their ideas for how to ask for help in an emergency.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.36 for Activity 1. Pupils read and analyse a short text to identify parts of a problem.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.36 for Activity 2. Pupils anticipate problems based on pictures to predict what they will hear.
Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.36 for Activity 3. Pupils listen for detail to see if they were correct in Step 4.

Based on the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.36 for Activity 4, have pupils work in pairs. Set up this activity as a role play, where one pupil plays the part of Mike Dobbs, and the other pupil gives him advice to solve the problem using expressions such as I think you should(n’t)… because… Remind pupils to explain the reasons for the advice they give. The advice should be based on what they hear in the listening activity. Replay this if necessary. (CCE: Values, helping others)
Ask some pupils to perform their role play to the class.
post: Choose a post-lesson task from Section 3 which reviews the content of the listening or language for giving advice, depending on the needs of your class.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 17 Exercise(s): 1–4 Workbook: Page: 15 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 36
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider giving pupils support at Step 6 to help them with ideas. You may also want to model the language by asking a more proficient pair to demonstrate to the class.

lessons.label: Speaking 2
lessons.focus: Reporting verbs (ways of speaking (e.g. whisper) & questions in the past (e.g. how did you feel?)

pre: Choose an activity from the Pre-lesson tasks in Section 3 to review key vocabulary for storytelling and reporting, such as -ed/-ing adjectives.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Vocabulary in the Teacher’s Book, p.34. Pupils work with definitions and use the dictionary at the back of the book. Remind them to use this dictionary when they need to, especially when they are reviewing the lessons at home.
Follow the instructions for Activities 1 & 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.34. Pupils match the sentences to pictures and then listen to check their answers.
Follow the instructions for Activities 3 & 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.34. Pupils listen and decide how the speaker is speaking then practice speaking in different ways.
Follow the instructions for Activity 5 in the Teacher’s Book, p.35. Pupils listen to the reporter’s questions and choose the best answers.
Pupils listen again to the questions. They write the questions they hear next to the answers in the Pupil’s Book (Activity 5, p.16).

Follow the instructions for Activity 6 in the Teacher’s Book, p.35. Pupils act out the emergency in small groups. Have them act as well as they can, showing emotion and using different voices. Encourage creativity in this activity (CCE: Creativity & Innovation).
Depending on time available, have one or more groups perform to the class.
post: Write a quote on the board from the story, using correct punctuation. Ask pupils to say the spoken text in different voices (e.g. whisper, shout, etc.)

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 16 Exercise(s): 1–6 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 34–35
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider assigning a director for Step 7, who helps the group act. They should use English for this but do not need to perform themselves.

lessons.label: Language Arts 3
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Verbs (e.g. wiggle, kick, tickle, lick, count, run, walk)

pre: Pupils look at their toes and describe them e.g. tiny, small, round, long, big
Elicit from pupils why they like their toes and what their toes can do.
delivery: Pupils recite the poem.
Ask pupils to act out the verbs in the poem.
Pupils trace their feet on a card and cut it out.
Pupils write a thank you note to their feet on the card.
Pupils arrange their feet cards around the class. Pupils walk around the class following the feet cards and read what their friends have written on their cards.
post: Pupils share their personal experiences on how to take care of their feet.

lessons.materials: Anthology of Poems for Year 4,5, and 6 Toes by Judith Nicholls Page: 30 Contemporary Children’s Literature Teaching Guidebook (BPK) – Poetry
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider providing pupils with additional support/phrases they can use in their note.

lessons.label: Language Awareness 1
lessons.focus: Teacher to complete:

std.note: Language Awareness lessons should be presented and practised using a Main Skill and a Complementary Skill (Listening, Speaking, Reading or Writing). Teachers can use Content and Learning Standards in the Year 6 DSKP.

pre: Review language from Unit 1 with an activity from the list of pre-lesson tasks in Section 3 or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14–17 for more ideas.
delivery: Choose from activities from the Workbook Check-up challenge, pp.16–17, which reviews the language, vocabulary and skills covered in this unit. This choice should be based on your observations and notes on pupils’ progress and achievement in these units. Choose activities which will review areas pupils found challenging or which they may have forgotten. You could have pupils choose for themselves what they would like to do in this review lesson. See Teacher’s Book, p.37 for instructions and answer keys for activities.

Have pupils do a Speaking task in pairs which is based on the Unit 1 or Welcome Unit theme. Monitor as they do this and note their performance. Note: ● Plan any further activities for this unit to develop language skills according to your pupils’ needs. ● You can use information about your pupils’ performance which you collected using formative assessment strategies while teaching this unit. ● The information could include your observation of pupils interacting in classroom activities and their performance in written activities. ● Plan activities which focus on language practice in a meaningful, fun and communicative way.
post: Ask pupils to think about their learning and performance in this unit. They then complete the self-assessment worksheet. Pupils should do this in English (see below).
Collect the worksheets from pupils and review them to note pupils’ responses. If there are any areas of concern, prepare a review of these in upcoming lessons.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 37 Workbook: Page(s): 16–17 Worksheet: A speaking task. Self-assessment worksheet (see below)
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. Ask pupils to do the self-assessment in English. Monitor and give support to less proficient pupils as needed.

lessons.label: Reading 3
lessons.focus: Used to / didn’t use to

pre: Show the pictures of London in the 17 th century and ask pupils what they can see, where they think it is, which century it is in, etc. Note any useful key vocabulary on the board.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book p.42. Use the picture of Samuel Pepys (pronounced: /piːps/) as you introduce pupils to him.
Follow instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.43. Pupils look at each picture and talk about what they see.
Follow instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.43. Pupils read to check their answers and to gain a global understanding of the text.
Follow instructions for Activity 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.43. Support and guide pupils as they develop the skill of guessing meaning from context.

Talk to pupils about how they record new vocabulary. You may have a system set up for this, such as using a special section of their notebooks, having a separate vocabulary notebook or using vocabulary cards (see Teacher’s Book, p.43). Encourage pupils to write definitions of new words in English and avoid translations unless necessary, especially in the case of more proficient pupils.

The Great Fire of London was a tragic event, but it helped eradicate the plague. Ask pupils to reflect on positive and negative outcomes of these events. (CCE: Global Sustainability). Support pupils in expressing their ideas in English by helping them with vocabulary and language if they speak in their home language.
post: Review new vocabulary in the lesson with an activity from the post-lesson tasks in Section 3 or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14–17, for more ideas.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 22–23 Exercise(s): 1–4 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 42–43 Pictures / illustrations of 17 th century London, the Great Fire of London and Samuel Pepys, if possible. Pictures / illustrations of any similar well-known events from local or national history
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider playing the recording as pupils read along in Step 4. This will help them to read more fluently as they won’t be able to keep stopping or stumbling over new words.

lessons.label: Listening 3
lessons.focus: Used to / didn’t use to

pre: Play a whole class or large group game using the nouns and verbs from Working With Words (Pupil’s Book, p.24). This could be ‘Listen and touch/run’, ‘Match on the board/large paper’, for example. Include write – writer. Ask pupils if they remember Samuel Pepys’ job (he was a writer).
delivery: Elicit some ideas from pupils about how people lived in London in Pepys’ time. Elicit more ideas about how pupils’ grandparents lived. Note useful ideas on the board.
Follow instructions for Vocabulary in the Teacher’s Book, p.48 to introduce vocabulary.

Follow instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.48. When asking questions to model used to, ask about pupils’ grandparents and/or Samuel Pepys. (CCE: Patriotism, finding out about local heritage).

Play the recording of the dialogue again. Have pupils listen for the pronunciation of used to (/'juːstə/). Point out that the pronunciation is different for use as a verb on its own. Drill several times chorally and individually, having pupils focus on their pronunciation while saying full positive and negative sentences and questions. Have pupils repeat in different voices to review whisper, shout, scream etc.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.48. Pupils use prompts to make a new dialogue.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.48. Pupils form questions using used to.
Drill the questions and check pupils’ pronunciation of used to again before having them practice the questions and answers (Activity 4, Pupil’s Book, p.26).
post: Follow the instructions for the Cooler Tic-tac-toe activity in the Teacher’s Book, p.48 or choose an activity from the post-lesson tasks to review areas of learning in this lesson that pupils have had difficulty with.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 24 & 26 Exercise(s): 1–4 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 48
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider drilling chorally as a whole class and then in pairs or small groups, rather than individually, if you have very shy pupils in your class.

lessons.label: Speaking 3
lessons.focus: Used to / didn’t use to

pre: Using the examples from pupils’ work from Lesson 18, say some sentences in the form they are written (pupils may have used present simple, past simple, or some may have used used to). In small groups, pupils listen and write a full sentence using used to when suitable. Repeat three or four times. Review and check as a whole class.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Warm-up: What can you see? in the Teacher’s Book, p.46, to focus attention on the language in context.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.46 to guide pupils to notice the target language form and meaning.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.46. Pupils complete the text using the target language.
Give pupils back their writing from Lesson 18. Have pupils use their similarities and differences to say sentences using used to/didn’t use to.

Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.46. Pupils talk to their partner about when they were three years old. Extend the activity by asking pupils to give one incorrect piece of information about themselves. Partners should guess which information is incorrect.

Individually, pupils write a short paragraph about their life in the past (e.g. when they were three years old). Set a word limit (see differentiation strategies) and consider having pupils finish for homework. Collect their work to evaluate their writing and language progress; adjust your upcoming teaching plans if you need to review particular areas or work more with individuals.
post: Consolidate learning with a speaking activity from the post-lesson tasks in Section 3.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 25 Exercise(s): 1–3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 46-47 Examples of past statements from pupils’ work from Lesson 18.
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider setting different targets for different pupils or allowing pupils to write as much (or as little) as they like. This will also give you formative feedback on motivation and attitude.

lessons.label: Language Arts 4
lessons.focus: Past simple tense

pre: Pupils look at Akbar’s Dream book cover and identify the features of the book cover e.g. title, author, blurb, publisher
delivery: Pupils look at the cover and brainstorm ideas on what the story is about.
Divide pupils into small groups and distribute a set of pictures from the guidebook (page 36) to each group.
In groups, pupils discuss the pictures and create a possible story based on the pictures given.
Groups take turns to narrate their predicted story to their classmates. Other groups provide feedback on their friends’ stories.
post: Pupils choose the story they think is most likely to happen. Teacher records the chosen predicted story and will revisit it once the pupils read and find out what happens.

lessons.materials: Akbar’s Dream by Jane Langford Akbar’s Dream Teacher’s Guidebook Page(s): 35-36
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. When grouping pupils, you can group pupils who can support each other in Step 3.

lessons.label: Writing 3
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Informal written language (e.g. Yuck!; Ha! Ha! Ha!)

pre: Choose an activity from the pre-lesson tasks in Section 3 to review the theme of Diaries refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book p.14–17 for more ideas.
delivery: Ask pupils to look again at the text on page 28 of the Pupil’s Book. Ask Whose diary is it? and Does Gemma use formal or informal language in her diary?

Follow the instructions for Activity 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.52. Pupils analyse the language in the diary. Remind pupils that exclamation marks are used more often in informal writing than in more formal writing. Ask pupils to find more examples of punctuation in the diary. Note that brackets are often used in informal writing to add information like the example.

Follow the instructions for Activity 5 in the Teacher’s Book, p.52. Pupils put their ideas together to help plan for Activity 6. If they have no shared experience of a trip, have them think about a family trip they have been on. Have them make written notes together, which they can use to support writing in the next step of the lesson. Monitor and help pupils.

Follow the instructions for Activity 6 in the Teacher’s Book, p.52. Pupils write a diary entry about a school trip. Either they write together or they can support each other if their content is different.
post: Follow the instructions for Learning to Learn in the Teacher’s Book, p.52.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 28–29 Exercise(s): 4–6 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 52
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider brainstorming some informal vocabulary with pupils before they write (e.g. adjectives such as really horrible, awesome, fantastic, awful) to help pupils express themselves fully. Consider preparing a model diary for Activity 6 (step 5) to support pupils in writing.

lessons.label: Speaking 4
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Review of past and future forms; Functional language – checking understanding (e.g. Can I check something, please?)

pre: Choose a pre-lesson task from the activities in Section 3 to review the main ideas from recent lessons, or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14–17 for more ideas.
delivery: Have pupils look at the functional language in the Pupil’s Book, p.30 (phrases to check understanding of what a speaker is saying). Ask them to copy the phrases into their notebooks, leaving two lines between each one. 2. Have pupils look back on their work during this unit. Hand out the worksheet. As they review their work, have them fill in the table with ideas they have had and information they have found out in the unit so far relating to life in the past, life now and life in the future.

Divide the class into two halves. Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.54. Note that half of the pupils should follow the task as described, and the other half should role play as a museum guide in the year you are in now (e.g. 2021) looking back at the past. As they do the activity, they should try to use the functional language. When they use it, they can tick it in their notebooks. They should aim to use each phrase at least once.

Introduce the idea of ‘presentism’, which suggests that people find it difficult to think about the past or future without basing their ideas on the present. You may need to use a little of the pupils’ home language to explain this concept. Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.55. Pupils discuss what they think will seem strange to people in the future about our lives in the present. Pupils discuss in pairs or small groups. (CCE: Values).

pre: Choose a Pre-lesson task from the list in Section 3 to review vocabulary from the current topic.
delivery: Tell pupils it was your birthday at the weekend (or talk about your real birthday). Tell them what you did on your birthday.
Draw a mind map on the board with headings such as Where? What? Why? Opinion? etc. (relating to the content of your talk). Pupils copy the mind map into their notebooks.
Tell pupils again about your birthday. They listen and complete mind map with notes.
Pupils compare their mind maps in pairs before some come out to complete the mind map on the board.

post: Choose a Cooler activity from the post-lesson tasks in Section 3 where pupils will be engaged in a fun, active game, or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14– 17 for more ideas.

Pupils cut each sheet into half, horizontally. Then, pupils cut out the pictures and excerpts to match them and arrange them in sequence.
Check pupils’ work before they paste the cut-outs onto the sheets of paper.
Pupils compile the sheets of paper to form a booklet and display their work in a gallery walk.
post: Use Post-lesson Task 8 (Test your memory): Have pupils review Chapter 2 for 1 minute. Hide one of the pictures of events and ask pupils to guess which picture is missing.

pre: Play a dictionary race, where you give pupils words to race to find in the dictionary. Choose words from the texts in Pupil’s Book, pp.48-49 but not those in the box on page 48.
delivery: Follow the instructions for the Warm-up activity in the Teacher’s Book p.80. Pupils brainstorm and think about different jobs.

Tell the pupils the text title (Unusual Jobs) and show the pictures from the Pupil’s Book pp.48-49. Pupils tell their partner what they think the texts will be about. Ask pupils if they can think of other unusual jobs.

lessons.label: Language Arts 8
lessons.focus: Punctuation: speech marks

delivery: Prepare cut-out speech strips from the guidebook (page 57) and put them in a box.
Select pupils randomly to pick out a speech strip. Pupils read out the speech strips using appropriate intonation and expression.
Other pupils guess the characters who said them and justify their answers by providing evidence from the text.
Distribute worksheets from the guidebook (page 58) to each pupil. Pupils complete the worksheets individually.
Have pupils check their answers in pairs, then as a whole class. Monitor and see how pupils manage the worksheets. Give feedback on their effort as much as their answers.

Monitor and see how pupils provide peer feedback.

lessons.label: Writing 6
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Tenses review; Adjectives to describe personality (e.g. brave); collocations with make and do (e.g. make a noise; do your homework).

pre: Remind pupils of the post-lesson activity you did in the last lesson (‘Numbers about me’). Have pupils do this activity in groups, using information about themselves.
delivery: Introduce vocabulary to describe personality (e.g. brave, shy, outgoing) which could describe people in different jobs. You could use examples for this.

Using the word/picture cards, pupils play a game in groups where they match adjectives and jobs (e.g. Pelmanism, where the cards are all face-down; in turns, pupils turn over two cards to see if they make a pair) (CCE: Values – Understanding that certain jobs require different personalities or qualities).

Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.90. However, pupils work first individually on their writing, basing it on their notes from the homework interview task (of course, they will have to change the title from ‘My English teacher’ to e.g. ‘My father’). They should add in a sentence at the end which describes the personality of the person they interviewed. If some pupils have not done the homework, they can write about you, as in the instructions in the Teacher’s Book.
Follow the instructions for Activity 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.90. Pupils self-evaluate their writing.
Have pupils make changes to their writing (second draft) in a different colour.
In groups, pupils volunteer to read their work to each other.
Follow the instructions for Working With Words in the Teacher’s Book, p.90. Pupils focus on collocations with make and do.
post: Consolidate learning in this lesson with a post-lesson task from Section 3 for this, or you could refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14–17.

pre: Write on the board: haven’t - I’m - time - I - sorry - had - . - , Pupils race to make a sentence [Answer: I’m sorry, I haven’t had time.] Repeat with another phrase from the previous lesson.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Communication in the Teacher’s Book, p.93. Extend this step by showing pupils how to keep interaction going to extend the dialogue, e.g. by repeating a speaker’s key words to check understanding or with phrases such as Do you mean…?
Follow the instructions for Activity 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.93. Pupils act out a dialogue with Robert. They should use strategies from Step 2 in their dialogue.

Hand out the worksheets and have pupils look at the dialogue and choose the most appropriate ways to complete it. They should work with expressions from this lesson at this stage, including polite language and interaction strategies.
In their notebooks, pupils draw a picture of a robot, and give it a name. The picture should show the robot doing something helpful (See Pupil’s Book, p.56 for a model).
Pupils use their robots to create and practise a similar dialogue to Step 3.
post: Have volunteers come to the front of the class to perform their dialogue. Give positive feedback on their efforts and draw attention in feedback to the use of interaction strategies (Main Leaning Standard).

lessons.label: Reading 7
lessons.focus: Spelling of common words, e.g. played, love, football

pre: Introduce pupils to the topic of codes by playing ‘Fizz-Bump’: Pupils stand in a circle (more than one circle if you have a large class) to play a counting game. In turns, going around the circle, they begin counting from 1. When a number can be divided by 3, pupils say fizz instead of the number; when divisible by 5, say bump. E.g.: (1) one – (2) two – (3) fizz – (4) four – (5) bump – (6) fizz (because 2x3=6) – (7) seven – (8) eight – (9) fizz (because 3x3=9) – (10) bump (because 2x5=10) and so on.
delivery: Reinforce the idea of codes by following the instructions for Cooler: Numbers and letters in the Teacher’s Book, p.95. Pupils should try to read words using a code. Note that this kind of code breaking supports pupils’ spelling.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.94. Pupils read and answer the questions.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.94. Pupils use the code to decode the message.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.94. Pupils create their own code in pairs.
Follow the instructions for Activity 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.94. Pupils write a message for their partner using the code.
Follow the instructions for Musical learners in the Teacher’s Book, p.94.
post: Follow the instructions for Warm-up in the Teacher’s Book, p.94. Pupils write words beginning with the letters in their names.

delivery: Pupils recite the poem aloud.

lessons.focus: Teacher to complete:

std.note: Language Awareness lessons should be presented and practised using a Main Skill and a Complementary Skill (Listening, Speaking, Reading or Writing). Teachers can use Content and Learning Standards in the Year 6 DSKP.

pre: Review language from Unit 4 with an activity from the list of pre-lesson tasks in Section 3 or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book pp.14–17 for more ideas.
delivery: Choose from activities from the Review section (Pupil’s Book pp.58–59, Activities 1–5), which reviews the language, vocabulary and skills covered in Units 3 and 4. This choice should be based on your observations and notes on pupils’ progress and achievement in these units. Choose activities which will review areas pupils found challenging or which they may have forgotten. You could have pupils choose for themselves what they would like to do in the review unit. See Teacher’s Book pp.96–97 for instructions for activities.

Have pupils do a listening task which is based on the unit theme of jobs. You can create your own script and read it aloud if you can’t find a suitable audio recording, or you could use a suitable video from the internet. Collect their work and note their performance. Note: ● Plan any further activities for this unit to develop language skills according to your pupils’ needs. ● You can use information about your pupils’ performance which you collected using formative assessment strategies while teaching this unit. ● The information could include your observation of pupils interacting in classroom activities and their performance in written activities. ● Plan activities which focus on language practice in a meaningful, fun and communicative way.
post: Ask pupils to think about their learning and performance in this unit. They then complete the self-assessment worksheet. Pupils should do this in English (see below).

lessons.label: Writing 7
lessons.focus: Cohesive devices (because, so, but)

pre: Review key vocabulary or ideas from the story in Lesson 65 that pupils found challenging using an activity from the pre-lesson task list in Section 3.
delivery: Ask pupils to remember the names of the characters in the story from Lesson 65. Then ask them about the theme of the story.

Follow instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.100. However, play a recording of the story or read it yourself, rather than have pupils read. Make sure that they sit comfortably, just as they did when they read the story in the last lesson.
Follow instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.100. Check answers and refer to the written text in Pupil’s Book, pp.60–61.

Highlight the use of because which links two ideas in a sentence in the examples in Activity 2 to give a reason. Elicit the meaning of so and but. Give pupils one or two examples to demonstrate and contrast the meaning of the words.

On the first worksheet, have pupils work in pairs to match the sentence halves on the worksheet. Then they add a suitable linking word, e.g. [Susi wanted to play inside] because [it was raining]. / [Grandma invented a cool robot] but [she couldn’t invent a flying machine.] / [Suddenly, the sun came out] so [Ruby went outside.]

Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.100. Pupils write their answers in full sentences using conjunctions (check they are punctuated properly), after discussing with their partner. Monitor and gather common mistakes to use in the post- lesson stage.
post: Use examples of pupils’ mistakes from Step 7 to conduct whole-class error correction on the board.

lessons.label: Writing 8
lessons.focus: Narrative tenses review, e.g. past simple, past continuous

pre: Gather pupils to the front of the classroom around you, or make sure they are sitting comfortably in their places. Tell the story you have chosen for this lesson. Make sure to include the beginning, middle and end. Ask a gist listening question to give pupils a reason to listen.
delivery: Ask pupils if they enjoyed listening to the story and give feedback on the gist question.

Tell pupils they will create their own stories in this lesson. Hand out the cut-up sentences from Pupil’s Book, p.67, one sentence per pupil. Note that these should be the first sentence given, not the questions and prompts, i.e. Tania sat up in bed. NOT She was excited because (Why?). Ask pupils to look at the picture and match their sentence to a picture.

Have pupils read the questions and prompts for their sentence on Pupil’s Book, p.67. In their notebooks, they write their sentence and then extend that stage of the story using the prompts given. They can answer these in any way they wish, even if it doesn’t exactly match the story.

Put pupils in groups of six so that the groups are made up of one pupil for each sentence/picture/stage of the story. Have pupils share their ideas to create a story. Note that the story may turn out oddly because it includes different ideas. Have pupils decide on a more logical progression of the story if necessary, although allow plenty of creativity and imagination – the story doesn’t have to be fixed.

Within the groups, pupils make pairs. In their notebooks, they work together to write the story. Allow plenty of time for this, and have pupils work together to co-write the story. Monitor and check pupils are participating equally.
post: Have volunteers read their stories to the class. The class should listen and identify any differences between what they hear and their own story.

pre: Show pupils a picture of a mother reprimanding her child.

lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider using the video, if available, in Step 2 to engage pupils who prefer to watch this.

lessons.label: Speaking 9
lessons.focus: Passive voice: questions (e.g. What’s it made of?) and statements (e.g. It’s made of…)

pre: Follow the instructions for Warm-up: Telephone in the Teacher’s Book, p.120.
delivery: Introduce the items and materials using the realia. Use the passive voice when talking about what the items are made of, e.g. this clock is made of glass and metal.
Play a game to practise the new vocabulary. You could choose an activity from the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14–17 or you could play a categorisation or brainstorming game/activity.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.120. Pupils hear the target language in context in the dialogue.
Follow instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.120. Pupils describe the objects.
Follow instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.120. Pupils make a new dialogue based on Activity 2.

Pupils work in groups. Give each group some realia. You could ask pupils to add to the realia using their own items. Pupils talk about the items they have, based on the model dialogue. Monitor and help with vocabulary. Also, check that all pupils are participating.
Give feedback by asking pupils to tell you what they have that is made of wood/metal/etc.
post: Play a guessing game where you describe items according to what they are made of and pupils guess what the items are, e.g. it is made of plastic, metal and glass. It is used for talking to people (answer: mobile phone).

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 74 Exercise(s):1–3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 120 Realia (real things) of a range of common items found in the home made of different materials. You could ask pupils to bring some unusual items from home.
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider asking each pupil to choose between two and five items to describe in Step 7. This would allow more proficient pupils to talk more, yet ensure less proficient or shy pupils also participate.

lessons.label: Language Arts 12
lessons.focus: First conditional, e.g. If you.., will..

pre: Write ‘Magic’ on the board and elicit responses from pupils on what they know about magic.
delivery: Go through the features of the book cover with pupils.
Pupils brainstorm ideas (characters, setting, story) about the book.
Pupils name themselves with special names (e.g. Jason the Joker, Henry the Handyman, Dave the Deejay)
Pose a question “If you become a Wizard what would you do?” Pupils share their ideas.
Pupils describe the special powers they want to have and the reasons for having the powers.
post: Pupils imagine and design a costume for themselves as a witch or wizard.

lessons.materials: The Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum The Wizard of Oz Teacher’s Guidebook
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider encouraging pupils to ask each other for help as well as asking you in Steps 5 and 6 in particular.

lessons.label: Writing 9
lessons.focus: Passive voice (e.g. Water is added to…); linking words (Sequencing: first, second, next, then, finally)

pre: Use an activity from the list of Pre-lesson tasks in Section 3 to review the topic of food and introduce ‘pasta’.
delivery: Look through the activities on pp.76–77 and note any vocabulary which is new for pupils. Write the new vocabulary on the board. Give different pairs two or three words to check in the dictionary or in the word list at the back of the Pupil’s Book (p.137).
Hand out the worksheets. Ask pairs to find the definitions for their words from Step 2.

Have pupils mingle in order to find out which words their classmates think match which definition. They will need to talk about the words they worked with in Steps 2 and 3. They should not show their worksheet, but should communicate in English to find out what their classmates think.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.124. Pupils match the stages with the pictures in the infographic and complete the sentences using the passive voice.
Give feedback on the answers for Step 5. Introduce or review linking words for sequencing at this stage (see Look! box in Pupil’s Book, p.77), focussing on the use of commas where appropriate.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.124. Pupils answer questions to guide them in writing an introduction.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.124. Pupils work in pairs to write about how pasta is made. Remind them to use linking words to help the flow of their writing.
post: Review and consolidate new vocabulary and target language from this lesson with an activity from the post-lesson tasks in Section 3 or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14–17 for more ideas.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 76–77 Exercise(s): 1–3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 124 Worksheet: Definitions for new vocabulary in this lesson. Dictionaries (optional)
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider nominating a few pupils to monitor in the mingling activity in Step 4 to remind pupils to speak English and not to show their worksheet to others.

lessons.label: Speaking 10
lessons.focus: Use of language in advertising, e.g. great value; wonderful; only $XX

pre: Review the topic of recent lessons, focussing on the previous lesson in particular. You could use an activity from the list of pre-lesson tasks from Section 3.
delivery: Show the adverts. Pupils decide what each advert is selling. They talk to their partner and note their answer.

Play the recording of the adverts in Pupil’s Book, Lesson 5 (Audio 1.28, see Teacher’s Book, p.122). Discuss with pupils the kind of language strategies used to try to encourage people to buy the product. This may be using strong words like love or fantastic, or telling people it is free or just.. (CCE: Values; Financial Education)
Have pupils look again at the Pupil’s Book, p.75, Activity 2 to identify how language is used to sell the products.
Show the adverts you brought again. Have pupils identify similar language. If it is in their L1, have them try to translate it into English.

Tell pupils they will work in groups to create and perform an advert (CCE: Creativity & Innovation). Assign groups and hand out the worksheet. Pupils put the steps in order so that they can complete the task, e.g. – decide what you will sell in your advert; - decide what language you will use to encourage people to buy it; - write a script; - practise your advert; - perform your advert. (CCE: Values).
Read out the steps of the project in order. Pupils listen and check their answers from Step 6. Focus pupils’ attention further on the guidelines in the Pupil’s Book, p.78, Activities 3 and 4.
Pupils prepare their adverts. Monitor to offer support and encouragement. Make sure pupils practise their adverts.
post: Groups perform their adverts to the class. Have the class evaluate them in terms of the kind of language they use and how effective the adverts are in selling the product. Manage this stage so that pupils give constructive comments and plenty of praise. (CCE: Values). Make a note of some of the feedback points, so you can refer to it in Lesson 94.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 75, 78 Exercise(s): 3–4 Audio 1.28 (See Teacher’s Book, p.122) Three or four adverts from magazines and/or TV. These could be in English and/or L1. Worksheet: Jumbled sentences giving the steps of the mini project to follow.
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, for Step 8, you may want to consider assigning one pupil per group to ensure everyone is on task and using English as appropriate.

lessons.label: Reading 10
lessons.focus: Functional language: giving opinions (e.g. For me, it’s important that…)

pre: Follow the instructions in the Teacher’s Book, p.128 for Warm-up: Ready, set, draw.
delivery: Review the topic of jeans by asking pupils if they wear jeans. Encourage them to talk about the small differences between jeans they wear (or other clothes).

Tell pupils they will read about some jeans and answer some reading comprehension questions. Pupils do the activity on the worksheet on their own. Monitor and note how pupils do on this activity, and discuss the answers as a whole class.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.128. Pupils read the texts (including the one they have just read) and complete the table.
Tell pupils how many RM (Malaysian Ringgits) there are in £1 (pound). Show them how to convert £ into RM. Have them convert the prices shown in the texts. (CCE: Financial Education).
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.128. Pupils talk about the different jeans.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.128. Pupils discuss how they would spend their £50. (CCE: Values).
post: Follow the instructions for Cooler: Football game, choose an activity from the post- lesson tasks in Section 3 or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book, pp.14–17 for more ideas.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 79 Exercise(s): 1–3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 128 Worksheet: Use one of the texts (Pupil’s Book. p.79) to create a reading comprehension assessment.
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider having less proficient pupils work with just one or two of the texts in Step 4.

lessons.label: Language Arts 13
lessons.focus: Future forms: will and going to

pre: Paste the enlarged version of ‘What is on the Cover’ worksheet from the guidebook on the board.
Pupils get into groups. In groups, pupils discuss and paste the answer cut-outs on the board.
Discuss the answers. The group with the most correct answers is the winner.
delivery: Each group performs group reading for Chapters 1 and 2.
Elicit responses from pupils about the setting, characters and how Dorothy’s house landed in the Land of Oz.
Pupils watch a short video of Dorothy in her blown away house. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RQWSh7Db-_E

Asks pupils the following questions: a. “If you were carried away by a cyclone like what happened to Dorothy, where do you think you will end up?” b. What will you see at the new place? c. What kind of characters will you meet?
Pupils complete the Circle Map worksheets. (Refer to guidebook page 100 -104)
Based on the three Circle Maps, pupils create a story that begins with: ‘If I was carried away by a cyclone like what happened to Dorothy, I think I would end up on…’
post: Pupils present their stories to the class.

lessons.materials: The Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum https://www.youtu be.com/watch?v= RQWSh7Db-_E The Wizard of Oz Teacher’s Guidebook Page(s): 32, 100-
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, in Step 9, you may want to consider providing marker or model sentences for weaker pupils. This will increase their chances of success by being able to write a story.

lessons.label: Language Awareness 5
lessons.focus: Teacher to complete:

std.note: Language Awareness lessons should be presented and practised using a Main Skill and a Complementary Skill (Listening, Speaking, Reading or Writing). Teachers can use Content and Learning Standards in the Year 6 DSKP.

pre: Review language from Unit 6 with an activity from the list of pre-lesson tasks in Section 3 or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book pp.14–17 for more ideas.
delivery: Choose from activities from the Review unit (Pupil’s Book pp.80–81, Activities 1–5), which review the language, vocabulary and skills covered in Units 5 and 6. This choice should be based on your observations and notes on pupils’ progress and achievement in these units. Choose activities which will review areas pupils found challenging or which they may have forgotten. You could have pupils choose for themselves what they would like to do in the review unit. See Teacher’s Book pp.130–131 for instructions for activities.

Have pupils do a reading task which is based on the unit theme. Collect their work and note their performance. Note: ● Plan any further activities for this unit to develop language skills according to your pupils’ needs. ● You can use information about your pupils’ performance which you collected using formative assessment strategies while teaching this unit. ● The information could include your observation of pupils interacting in classroom activities and their performance in written activities. ● Plan activities which focus on language practice in a meaningful, fun and communicative way.
post: Ask pupils to think about their learning and performance in this unit. They then complete the self-assessment worksheet. Pupils should do this in English (see below).
Collect the worksheets from pupils and review them to note pupils’ responses. If there are any areas of concern, prepare a review of these in upcoming lessons.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 80–81 Exercise(s): 1–5 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 130–131 Worksheet: A reading task. Self-assessment worksheet (see below).
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. Ask pupils to do the self-assessment in English. Monitor and give support to less proficient pupils as needed.

lessons.label: Writing 10
lessons.focus: Adjectives to describe personality; prefixes: im- / un- / dis-

pre: Follow the instructions for Warm-up: One-question interview in the Teacher’s Book, p.132.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.134. Pupils review the reading text from the previous lesson and answer questions in Pupil’s Book, p.84.

Elicit and tell pupils more about the legend of Robin Hood, an English folk legend. Focus in particular on how he helped people and was a hero (CCE: Values). You could show a picture of Robin Hood or even an extract from one of many films about him.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.134. Pupils think about the focus and features of the two texts.
Follow the instructions for Working with words in the Teacher’s Book, p.134. Pupils look at modifying words in order to make them negative.
Ask pupils to highlight words which relate to personality. Brainstorm more adjectives to describe personality.
In pairs, have pupils use some of the words to describe Robin Hood. They discuss their ideas first.
Then, have pairs of pupils write at least four sentences to describe the personality of Robin Hood. Focus on the adjectives in particular and have pupils check spelling.
Pairs share and discuss their ideas with another pair to see if they agree.
post: Play a short extract from a Robin Hood film and ask pupils to check their personality adjectives. Or you could use the personality adjectives in a personalised activity, such as one from the list of post-lesson tasks in Section 3.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 82–84 Exercise(s): 1–2 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 132, 134 Picture of Robin Hood and/or extract from a Robin Hood film.
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider the extension activity in the Teacher’s Book on p.135.

lessons.label: Listening 10
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Present simple for future meaning

pre: Review the texts from the previous lesson by asking Questions 2 and 3 in Activity 3 in the Pupil’s Book, p.84. (CCE: Patriotism)
delivery: Ask pupils if they have ever been to or performed in a music concert to set the context of the dialogue.
Follow the instructions for Vocabulary in the Teacher’s Book, p.138.

Show the picture in the Pupil’s Book, p.86 to further set the context, then hand out the worksheet. Ask pupils to close their books (so they can’t read) and then have them listen to the recording of the dialogue (See Teacher’s Book, p.138/Pupil’s Book, p.86, Audio 2.2) and answer the questions individually.
Pupils check their answers in pairs before reviewing them as a class. Note any problems pupils have with this style of question, or individuals who found this particularly challenging.
Draw pupils’ attention to the future meaning in the use of present form, e.g. The bus leaves at 6.30 – is 6.30 now, or in the future?
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.138. Pupils make statements in the present simple for future meaning.
Follow instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.138. Pupils make and practise similar dialogues.
post: Follow the instructions for Cooler: Itinerary in the Teacher’s Book, p.139.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 84, 86 Exercise(s): 3, 1– 3 Audio 2.2 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 138–139 Worksheet: A listening task: MCQs for the dialogue (Pupil’s Book, p.86, Activity 1).
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider supporting less proficient pupils in listening by allowing them to refer to the script in the Pupil’s Book as they answer the questions on the worksheet.

lessons.label: Speaking 11
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Future forms: will and going to

pre: Follow the instructions for Warm-up: Tense review in the Teacher’s Book, p.136.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.136. Pupils are introduced to will and going to futures. Contrast with the use of present simple, which we use for scheduled future events.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.136. Pupils complete the sentences with will or going to.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.137. Pupils discuss the questions.
Ask pupils to write about their future ideas in Activity 3 in the Workbook, p.74. You could make a worksheet based on this.
In pairs, pupils talk about their ideas in Step 5. Encourage them to ask each other extension questions.
post: Discuss the Values question in the Pupil’s Book, p.85 (See Teacher’s Book, p.137) with the class, then have them brainstorm ideas in small groups. (CCE: Values)

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 85 Exercise(s): 1–3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 136–137 Workbook: Page: 74 Exercise: 3
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider focussing on meaning rather than using grammatical terminology in Step 1 if pupils are less familiar with tense names in English.

lessons.label: Language Arts 14
lessons.focus: Narrate short stories, events and experiences

pre: Use Pre-lesson Task 5 (Sit down, Stand Up): Teacher comes up with statements that may be true or false from Chapters 1 and 2 of The Wizard of Oz. Pupils stand up if the statement is true and sit down if the statement is false (e.g. Dorothy lived on a prairie in Kansas- true)
delivery: In groups, pupils read Chapters 3 and 4 and discuss the main events in the chapters.
Each group is given a description of a scene from the chapters read.
Pupils discuss in their respective groups and come up with a short act to depict the scenes.
Groups take turns to act out and pupils guess the scenes.
post: Pupils assess each group’s presentation using Two Stars and a Wish: two things that are good (stars) and one thing that can be improved (wish).

lessons.materials: The Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum The Wizard of Oz Teacher’s Guidebook Page(s): 85-86
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, in Steps 4-5, you may want to consider assigning a director who helps the group act. They should use English for this but do not need to perform themselves.

lessons.label: Writing 11
lessons.focus: Phonology: rhythm and rhyme

pre: Play a rhyming game, where pupils hear a word and should say another word which rhymes.
delivery: Re-elicit and write some of the pairs of rhyming words on the board from p.88 of the Pupil’s Book. Remind pupils that sometimes the spelling is consistent between the pairs (e.g. same & game), but other times it is different (e.g. first & worst).
Play the song from Lesson 102 again. Have pupils read along in the Pupil’s Book, p.88 as they listen.
Ask pupils to identify the rhyming words in the song.
Follow the instructions for Activity 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.142-143. Pupils use a word in the box to complete the song.
Have pupils try to write another verse for the song using their own ideas.
Follow the instructions for Activity 5 in the Teacher’s Book. Note that pupils’ verses could be very different from one another’s.
post: Ask for volunteers to sing their verse to the class. Ask for feedback on the rhythm and rhyme in particular.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 88–89 Exercise(s): 4–5 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 142-143
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider having pupils use the model in Activity 4 to write another verse in Step 6 if they need it. More proficient pupils could write a completely new verse.

lessons.label: Listening 11
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Describing music (e.g. catchy)

pre: Review the topic of music and concerts using an activity from the pre-lesson tasks in Section 3.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book. Pupils are introduced to the content of the listening.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book. Pupils listen to check their predictions in Step 2.

Draw attention to the words in the box at the top of Pupil’s Book, p.87. Ask pupils to guess the meaning of the words, based on what they have heard so far. Have pupils listen again for the words and try to guess their meaning. Finally, have them check meaning in the dictionary on p.140 of the Pupil’s Book.

Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.140. Pupils listen for specific information to answer the questions. Encourage pupils to read and predict the gapped answers before listening. Note that this strategy is useful for the listening assessment.

Explain that pupils will do a reading activity. Hand out the worksheets and have pupils read the questions. Elicit and discuss strategies for this question type, such as looking at different parts of the sentences in each option to check it matches with both what comes before and after it; and looking at the whole dialogue to get an overall understanding of the context so that the dialogue will make sense.

Have pupils answer the questions individually before checking in pairs, then in the whole class. Monitor and see how pupils manage the questions. Give feedback on their effort as much as their answers.
post: Review the music theme from the lesson by asking which song from the listening text sounds best. Have pupils justify their answers. Ask pupils to bring a recording of their favourite song to the next lesson on CD, audio file or link, if possible, so they can play it to the class.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 87 Exercise(s): 1–3 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 140 Worksheet: A reading activity using a dialogue similar to Activity 1 in the Pupil’s Book, p.86 about a concert by one of the three singers on p.87.
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider using guiding questions to help pupils understand the words in Step 4, such as: Does Clare like the song? Do you think this adjective is positive or negative? What word/suffix can you see?

lessons.label: Reading 11
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: Emotions (e.g. frightened, happy)

pre: Play a game to introduce the topic of films. You could choose an activity from the list of
tasks in Section 3.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Warm-up: Tell me about it! in the Teacher’s Book, p.146. Pupils talk about a film they saw recently.
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.146. Pupils look at scripts and match them to types of film.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.146. Pupils listen to some music and say how it makes them feel.
Model reading aloud with emotion, as if acting in a film, using the scripts in Activity 1. Ask pupils to talk about how we can put emotion into what we say.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.146. Pupils match the music to the film type.
Have pupils practice the different scripts in pairs. Encourage them to act using mime and gesture as they would if they are acting.
Ask for volunteers for Activity 4. See the Teacher’s Book. p.146
post: Follow the instructions for Cooler: Which instruments? In the Teacher’s Book, p.147.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 91 Exercise(s): 1–4 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 146–147
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to avoid nominating pupils to perform in front of the class as some pupils in the class may feel inhibited or shy. These pupils may also prefer not to act, even in Step 7. Avoid making them do so if they’d prefer not to.

lessons.label: Language Arts 15
lessons.focus: Adjectives

pre: Conduct a pop quiz on the traits of each character in the story (Refer to guidebook page 68).
delivery: In small groups, pupils read out Chapters 5, 6 and 7.
Elicit responses from the pupils about the characters and their actions in the story.
Explain to pupils that they will write an acrostic poem.
In groups, pupils choose a character and discuss the characteristics as well as the significant dialogues.
Pupils write acrostic poems based on their chosen characters.
post: Pupils recite their acrostic poems.
Conduct class feedback.

lessons.materials: The Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum The Wizard of Oz Teacher’s Guidebook Page(s): 60-62
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider monitoring less proficient pupils more closely to offer support and encouragement and check their understanding of the tasks.

lessons.label: Language Awareness 6
lessons.focus: Teacher to complete:

std.note: Language Awareness lessons should be presented and practised using a Main Skill and a Complementary Skill (Listening, Speaking, Reading or Writing). Teachers can use Content and Learning Standards in the Year 6 DSKP.

pre: Review language from Unit 7 with an activity from the list of Pre-lesson tasks in Section 3 or refer to the Games Bank in the Teacher’s Book p.14-17 for more ideas.
delivery: Choose from activities from the Workbook Check-up Challenge p.80-81, which reviews the language, vocabulary and skills covered in this unit. This choice should be based on your observations and notes on pupils’ progress and achievement in these units. Choose activities which will review areas pupils found challenging or which they may have forgotten. You could have pupils choose for themselves what they would like to do in this review lesson. See Teacher’s Book p.147 for instructions and answer keys for activities.

Depending on your pupils’ needs, have them do a writing task or a reading task which is based on the unit theme. Collect their work and note their performance. Note: ● Plan any further activities for this unit to develop language skills according to your pupils’ needs. ● You can use information about your pupils’ performance which you collected using formative assessment strategies while teaching this unit. ● The information could include your observation of pupils interacting in classroom activities and their performance in written activities. ● Plan activities which focus on language practice in a meaningful, fun and communicative way.

Collect the worksheets from pupils and review them to note pupils’ responses. If there are any areas of concern, prepare a review of these in upcoming lessons.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Workbook: Page(s): 80–81 Worksheet: A writing task or a reading task. Self-assessment worksheet (see below).
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. Ask pupils to do the self-assessment in English. Monitor and give support to less proficient pupils as needed.

lessons.label: Reading 12
lessons.focus: 1 st conditional if clauses. (If + present, will + vb, e.g. If you ask him, he’ll paint…)

pre: Choose an activity from the pre-lesson tasks which introduces the topic of stories. You could also ask pupils what their favourite story is.
delivery: Follow the instructions for Warm-up: Famous Characters in the Teacher’s Book, p.152. Encourage pupils to think of stories in their own culture as well as in other cultures. (CCE: Patriotism).
Follow the instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.152. Pupils look at the picture to get an idea of the topic and setting of the story before reading through a prediction task.
Follow the instructions for Activity 2 in the Teacher’s Book, p.152. Have pupils relax and sit comfortably to read the story in their own time, rather than rush through it.
Follow the instructions for Activity 3 in the Teacher’s Book, p.153. Pupils decide on the main message of the story.

Talk to pupils about stories with a message. Elicit other stories from their own culture and others (e.g. Aesop’s Fables) which have a message. Explain how, in the past, adults educated children in morality through stories from a young age. (CCE: Values).

Follow the instructions for Activity 4 in the Teacher’s Book, p.153. Pupils guess the meaning of new words from the context of the story. Have pupils look at as many of the words as they can within a set time limit.
post: Follow the instructions for Cooler: What’s the word? in the Teacher’s Book, p.152.

lessons.materials: Academy Stars Year 6 Pupil’s Book: Page(s): 96–97 Exercise(s): 1–4 Teacher’s Book: Page(s): 152–153
lessons.differentiation: Differentiate learning according to the needs of your pupils. Please see the seven differentiation strategies in Section 4. In addition, you may want to consider having a quiet task for fast readers to do in Step 4 so that they are quiet while other pupils finish reading the story.

lessons.label: Listening 12
lessons.theme: World of Self, Family and Friends
lessons.focus: 1 st conditional if clauses (If + present, will + verb: If you rest, you’ll feel better)

pre: Choose a pre-lesson task from the list in Section 3 which introduces the idea of if clauses.
delivery: Follow instructions for Warm-up: Future predictions in the Teacher’s Book, p.156. Pupils make predictions in pairs using will.
Follow instructions for Activity 1 in the Teacher’s Book, p.156. Pupils are introduced to the new target language.

Use the sentences in Activity 2 in the Pupil’s Book, p.99 to make some correct/incorrect sentences. Have pupils close their books.
